flags: The three NCDOT cache files have identical extracted bodies ending during Historic Flat Rock, before the Drover’s Road chapter. Its table of contents confirms inclusion but not the specific scenic rationale, endpoints, curves, grades, overlooks or travel time. No claim of present uninterrupted access is made.

Dropped unsupported current claims: beginning at the Blue Ridge Parkway; crossing Hickory Nut Gap; mature hillside trees and rhododendron-covered gorge walls; Hickory Nut Creek also called Rocky Broad; Little Pisgah Mountain’s 4,412-foot height, eastward visibility and Konnatoga name; Sherrill’s Inn serving settlers, drovers and Civil War soldiers, giving the gap its former name, and being a private home visible on wide curves.

Little Pisgah Mountain moment removed because no cache page supplies a story about that peak; Little Pisgah Point in the preserve is a different named feature. Florence Nature Preserve replaces it. Material has no strip towns; order follows the retained coordinates and US 74A community geography.
Sherrill’s Inn’s about-1845 building date is distinct from the unsupported 1834–1909 business dates in material. The cache supplies no verified roadside view or visitor arrangements.
The Gerton postal-error story has only a secondary source. Its claimed embarrassment and Freeman’s personality were omitted; a postal or local historical record would strengthen verification.

Bat Cave cache/12.txt records significant Hurricane Helene damage in 2024, while the NCDOT guide is dated 2021. Current road and preserve access cannot be established from these files; editor needs a newer manager source.
